chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdis-Salam ibn Saleh al-Harawi that he had heard Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) say:

I shall be murdered by poison as a victim of injustice, and I will be buried next to Harun. God will establish my grave as the place for visiting by my followers and those who love me. Whoever visits me in my loneliness, then visiting him on the Resurrection Day will become incumbent upon me. By Him who honored Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with the Prophetic mission and chose him over all his creatures, whichever one of you who says two units of prayers next to my tomb will deserve to be forgiven by God the Honored the Exalted on the Day you meet Him. And by Him who honored us with the Divine Leadership mission after Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and made us especial by granting us the Testamentary Trustee mission, whoever visits my shrine will be of the noblest ones who reach God on the Resurrection Day. God the Highest keeps away the Fire from the corpse of any believer who visits me, hits himself on the face and sheds a tear.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits of visiting the grave of Imam Ar-Ridha according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (a.s.) foretells his martyrdom by poison at the hands of the Abbasid caliph al-Ma'mun and his subsequent burial in the Khurasan cemetery next to Harun al-Rashid. He establishes the theological significance of his shrine as a locus of divine mercy, promising that visiting his grave—even in his 'absence' or *ghurba*—secures guaranteed intercession and protection from the Fire, reinforcing the Shia concept of the Imam's enduring spiritual presence.
